chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
An orphan was brought to Amir al-Mu'minin (blessings of Allah upon him), and he said: 'Let the closest person to him from his clan bear his expenses, just as they would consume his inheritance.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful; title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.الْعَشِيرَة: Clan or extended tribal family; the wider kinship group beyond the immediate household
key_terms.مِيرَاث: Inheritance; property transmitted by Islamic inheritance laws (mirath/faraid)
key_terms.نَفَقَة: Financial maintenance/support; a legal obligation in Islamic law covering food, clothing, and shelter

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for the financial maintenance of an orphan in Islamic law according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that when an orphan was presented before Imam Ali (AS), he ruled that the financial maintenance of the orphan should be the responsibility of the nearest relative from the clan — the same person who would be entitled to inherit from the orphan. This ruling establishes a principle of reciprocity in Islamic family law: the right to inherit entails the corresponding obligation to provide financial support. The ruling was addressed to those around Ali (AS), reinforcing that the Islamic legal system obligates those with inheritance claims to also bear caretaking responsibilities.
